hook.text: The Mariana Trench plunges nearly 11 kilometers deep—if Everest were placed inside, it would still be submerged.

buildup.text: Trenches form where one tectonic plate dives beneath another in a process called subduction.

discovery.text: The deepest point, Challenger Deep, was first reached in 1960 by Piccard and Walsh.

twist.text: Plastic bags have been found at the bottom of the Mariana Trench—pollution reaches everywhere.

climax.text: Trenches are also earthquake factories—subduction generates the world's most powerful quakes.

punchline.text: The deepest places on Earth are where the seafloor is swallowed.

quiz.question: How do ocean trenches form?
options: One tectonic plate dives beneath another
